# Put Resource

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/put_resource_resources__resourceid__put.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Put Resource

Update properties of an existing resource.
If the resource does not exist, a new resource will be created

# OpenAPI definition

````json
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Eratos Workspace API",
    "description": "## Getting started\n### Authentication\n\nThe Eratos Workspace API uses _Basic Authentication_ and _Bearer Token Authentication_ to authenticate requests.\n\n#### Basic Authentication\n\nTo authenticate with the Eratos Workspace API using _Basic Authentication_, an Eratos `key` and `secret` is required.\n\nVisit Eratos Workspace: [https://workspace.eratos.com/development](https://workspace.eratos.com/development) to generate Eratos credentials\n\n`Basic` Authentication typically requires a `username` and `password` to be sent in the `Authorization` request header however instead a `key` and `secret` is used:\n\n```http\nAuthorization: Basic <key:secret>\n```\n\n`<key:secret>` is a placeholder that represents a base64 encoded string. Most request libraries will generate a base64 string for you automatically.\n\n#### Example\nTo test locally, run the example below replacing `your_key` and `your_secret` with your `key` and `secret`.\n\n```bash\n> echo -n your_key:your_secret | base64 -w 0\neW91cl9rZXk6eW91cl9zZWNyZXQ=\n> curl https://api.eratos.com/api/workspace/v1/resources -H \"Authorization: Basic eW91cl9rZXk6eW91cl9zZWNyZXQ=\"\n```\n\n> Basic Authentication requires HTTPS to keep the credentials secure while in transit.\n\n    \n### Key Concepts:\n#### Identifiers\n* `ern` (Eratos Resource Name)\n    \n    A ERN is a globally unique identifier that identifies a resource within the Eratos ecosystem. It is a structured string that identifies a `resource`, `schema`, `policy`, `user`, `account`, or `node`. \n    \n    *Structure of an `ern`:*\n    \n    - `ern:{node}:{type}:{id}`\n        - `{node}` - identifies the location or lookup address of a resource. May blank if the resource is not location specific.\n        - `{type}`: - the type of entity this ern represents\n            - `resource` \n            - `node`\n            - `schema`\n            - `policy`\n            - `user`\n            - `account`\n        - `{id}`: - the unique identifier of the `ern`\n            - Either:\n                - 24 character alpha-numeric (e.g. `XYZABC123456ABCDEF123456`)\n                - A prefixed custom id (common id) in the form `{namespace}.{customer_id}`\n            - examples:\n                - `ern:e-pn.io:resource:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`\n                - `ern:e-pn.io:resource:eratos.block.test`\n                - `ern::node:e-pn.io`\n                - `ern:e-pn.io:schema:space`\n                - `ern::user:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`\n                - `ern::account:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`\n#### Eratos Entities            \n* `resource` - Provides structured metadata about a _thing_ or a _concept_.\n    * Every resource has the following minimum required properties:\n        * `@id` - the identifying `ern` of the resource\n        * `@type` - the `schema` of the resource identified by a `schema ern`\n        * `@owner` - the owner of a resource identified by an `ern`. Can be a `user` or `resource` `ern`.\n        * `@policy` - the `policy` that applies to the `resource` identified by a `policy ern`\n    * Additional properties are defined by the `schema` of the resource.        \n* `schema` - Defines the structure of a `resource` including the properties and constraints.\n* `policy` - A set of rules that govern the access to a `resource` or `node`\n* `node` - Either be a _Primary_ or a _Gateway_ node identified by a `node ern`\n    * _Primary Node_ - Provides management of `resources`, `policies`, and `schemas`.\n        * Eratos Managed Primary Node: `ern::node:e-pn.io`\n    * _Gateway Node_ - Provides access to raw data and additional query processing services.\n        * Eratos Managed Gateway Node: `ern::node:au-1.e-gn.io`\n* `user` - A user identified by a `user ern`\n* `account` - An account or billing entity identified by an `account ern`\n\n## Support\nFor any support-related questions or feature requests, please contact:\n\n- **Support Team**: support@eratos.com\n\n",
````

# Drill Dataset

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/drill_dataset_drill_get.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Drill Dataset

Drill a gridded dataset at a given latitude and longitude along the time axis for a given variable or variables
        
- If no variables are provided, all variables in the dataset will be returned. To obtain a list of variables in the dataset, see the `/resources/:rid` endpoint.
- Results are returned in natural order by default, however, the `direction` parameter can be used to reverse the order of the results
- Limits and offsets can be used to paginate the results (default limit is 10 and max limit is 1000)
        
Constraints: 
- Only resources of type `ern:e-pn.io:schema:block` or `ern:e-pn.io:schema:dataset` are supported and must offer a gridded interface.
- The dataset resource must have a recognised time property to drill on. Supported property names are ['time']
- The dataset resource must have a recognised `latitude` and `longitude` property to drill on. Supported property names are ['lat', 'latitude', 'Latitude'] and ['lon', 'longitude', 'Longitude']
- The `start` date must be before the `end` date if both are provided and in ISO8601 format
- The `latitude` must be between -90 and 90 degrees and the longitude must be between -180 and 180 degrees inclusive.
- The `latitude` and `longitude` must be within the bounds of the dataset
            
Returns: 
- A timeseries along the time axis for the given latitude and longitude with the requested variables
        
Example:
            
```
GET /drill?resourceId=eratos.blocks.silo.maxtemperature&variable=max_temp&latitude=-37.8&longitude=144.95&start=2024-08-23&end=2024-08-24
```

# Subset Geospatial Dataset

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/subset_geospatial_dataset_subset_get.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Subset Geospatial Dataset

> 🧪 **Beta Feature**: The subset endpoint is currently in beta testing, the API query parameters and response formats are subject to change. If you have any feedback please contact us through our [support portal](https://eratos.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/2).

Subset a gridded dataset within a bounding box of latitude and longitude coordinates along the time axis for a given variable or variables

- If no variables are provided, all variables in the dataset will be returned. To obtain a list of variables in the dataset, see the `/resources/:rid` endpoint.
- Results are returned in natural order by default, however, the `direction` parameter can be used to reverse the order of the results
- Limits and offsets can be used to paginate the results (default limit is 10 and max limit is 10000)
- Results can be returned in different formats based on the Accept header (application/json, image/tiff, application/vnd.eratos.json)

Constraints: 
- Only resources of type `ern:e-pn.io:schema:block` or `ern:e-pn.io:schema:dataset` are supported and must offer a gridded interface.
- The dataset resource must have a recognised time property to subset on. Supported property names are ['time']
- The dataset resource must have recognised `latitude` and `longitude` properties to subset on. Supported property names are ['lat', 'latitude', 'Latitude'] and ['lon', 'longitude', 'Longitude']
- The `start` date must be before the `end` date if both are provided and in ISO8601 format
- The bounding box coordinates must be within valid ranges: latitude between `-90` and `90` degrees, longitude between `-180` and `180` degrees
- The bounding box must be specified in the order of `minLongitude,minLatitude,maxLongitude,maxLatitude`
- Only 3-dimensional datasets are supported
- The dimensional selection must not exceed 10000 cells
- When requesting image/tiff format, only one variable can be specified

Returns: 
- A spatiotemporal subset within the specified bounding box with the requested variables
- Format depends on the Accept header
  - JSON by default (application/json)
  - JSON, no href links (application/vnd.eratos.json)
  - GeoTIFF (image/tiff)

Example:
Gets the last 10 results from the dataset from the given coordinates for `max_temp`
```
GET /subset?resourceId=eratos.blocks.silo.maxtemperature&bbox=144.95,-37.8,145.05,-37.7&variable=max_temp&limit=10&skip=0&direction=-1
```

# Eratos Workspace API (v1)

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/eratos-workspace-api-v1.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Eratos Workspace API (v1)

https://api.eratos.com/api/workspace/v1/

## Getting Started

### Authentication

The Eratos Workspace API uses *Basic Authentication* and *Bearer Token Authentication* to authenticate requests.

#### Basic Authentication

To authenticate with the Eratos Workspace API using *Basic Authentication*, an Eratos `key` and `secret` is required.

Visit Eratos Workspace: <https://workspace.eratos.com/development> to generate Eratos credentials

`Basic` Authentication typically requires a `username` and `password` to be sent in the `Authorization` request header however instead a `key` and `secret` is used:

```http
Authorization: Basic key:secret
```

`key:secret` is a placeholder that represents a base64 encoded string. Most request libraries will generate a base64 string for you automatically.

#### Example

To test locally, run the example below replacing `your_key` and `your_secret` with your `key` and `secret`.

```bash
echo -n your_key:your_secret | base64 -w 0
eW91cl9rZXk6eW91cl9zZWNyZXQ=
curl https://api.eratos.com/api/workspace/v1/resources -H \"Authorization: Basic eW91cl9rZXk6eW91cl9zZWNyZXQ=\"
```

> Basic Authentication requires HTTPS to keep the credentials secure while in transit.

### Key Concepts:

#### Identifiers

* `ern` (Eratos Resource Name)\
  A ERN is a globally unique identifier that identifies a resource within the Eratos ecosystem. It is a structured string that identifies a `resource`, `schema`, `policy`, `user`, `account`, or `node`.\
  *Structure of an`ern`:*
  * `ern:{node}:{type}:{id}`
    * `{node}` - identifies the location or lookup address of a resource. May blank if the resource is not location specific.
    * `{type}`: - the type of entity this ern represents
      * `resource`
      * `node`
      * `schema`
      * `policy`
      * `user`
      * `account`
    * `{id}`: - the unique identifier of the `ern`
      * Either:
        * 24 character alpha-numeric (e.g. `XYZABC123456ABCDEF123456`)
        * A prefixed custom id (common id) in the form `{namespace}.{customer_id}`
      * examples:
        * `ern:e-pn.io:resource:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`
        * `ern:e-pn.io:resource:eratos.block.test`
        * `ern::node:e-pn.io`
        * `ern:e-pn.io:schema:space`
        * `ern::user:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`
        * `ern::account:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`

#### Eratos Entities

* `resource` - Provides structured metadata about a *thing* or a *concept*.
  * Every resource has the following minimum required properties:
    * `@id` - the identifying `ern` of the resource
    * `@type` - the `schema` of the resource identified by a `schema ern`
    * `@owner` - the owner of a resource identified by an `ern`. Can be a `user` or `resource` `ern`.
    * `@policy` - the `policy` that applies to the `resource` identified by a `policy ern`
  * Additional properties are defined by the `schema` of the resource.
* `schema` - Defines the structure of a `resource` including the properties and constraints.
* `policy` - A set of rules that govern the access to a `resource` or `node`
* `node` - Either be a *Primary* or a *Gateway* node identified by a `node ern`
  * *Primary Node* - Provides management of `resources`, `policies`, and `schemas`.
    * Eratos Managed Primary Node: `ern::node:e-pn.io`
  * *Gateway Node* - Provides access to raw data and additional query processing services.
    * Eratos Managed Gateway Node: `ern::node:au-1.e-gn.io`
* `user` - A user identified by a `user ern`
* `account` - An account or billing entity identified by an `account ern`

## Support

For any support-related questions or feature requests, please contact:

* **Support Team**: <support@eratos.com>

Terms of service: <https://www.eratos.com/license-terms>

# Deletes a data file from Thredds

# Deletes a data file from Thredds

Deletes a data file from Thredds.

The dataset to delete can be identified in one of two ways: either using the dataset's URL path, or using its ID. If identifying the dataset by its URL path, the ID of the organisation owning the dataset **must** be given as the first component of the `path` parameter, or via the `organisationid` parameter (but not both).

This operation differs from the `deleteDataByPath` operation only in how the `path` is passed: in this case, the `path` is passed as a query parameter.

# Uploads a new data file to Thredds

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/postdata.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Uploads a new data file to Thredds

Uploads a new data file to Thredds.

Files uploaded using this service are placed in an organisation-specific catalog, and their URL path is prefixed with the uploading organisation's ID. As a concrete example, if uploading a new data file to be owned by an organisation 'Acme' (e.g. `organisationid=acme`) and with `path=/some/directory/file.nc`, then the final URL path of the uploaded file will be `/acme/some/directory/file.nc`, and the details of the file will be found in an Acme-specific catalog that will be linked from the main Thredds catalog.

# Replaces an existing data file in Thredds

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/reference/putdata.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Replaces an existing data file in Thredds

Replaces an existing data file in Thredds.

Files uploaded using this service replace an existing dataset.The path is prefixed with the dataset's existing organisation id, similar to the POST `/data` operation. As a concrete example, if uploading a  data file owned by the organisation 'Acme' (e.g. `organisationid=acme`) and with `path=/some/directory/file.nc`, then the final URL path of the uploaded file will be `/acme/some/directory/file.nc`, and the details of the file will be found in an Acme-specific catalog that will be linked from the main Thredds catalog.

# OpenAPI definition

```json
{
```

> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt

# Deletes a data file from Thredds

Deletes a data file from Thredds.

The dataset to delete can be identified in one of two ways: either using the dataset's URL path, or using its ID. If identifying the dataset by its URL path, the ID of the organisation owning the dataset **must** be given as the first component of the `path` parameter, or via the `organisationid` parameter (but not both).

This operation differs from the `deleteDataByPath` operation only in how the `path` is passed: in this case, the `path` is appended to the request path.

# OpenAPI definition

# Assess Property Viability

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/recipes/assess-property-viability.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Assess Property Viability

```python Python
import datetime
from datetime import timezone
import pandas as pd
from pyparsing import alphas
from shapely import wkt, geometry
from eratos.creds import AccessTokenCreds
from eratos.adapter import Adapter
from eratos.resource import Resource
import time
from shapely import wkt, geometry
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from tabulate import tabulate

ecreds = AccessTokenCreds(
  "YOUR_KEY_ID_GOES_HERE",
  "YOUR_KEY_SECRET_GOES_HERE"
)
eadapter = Adapter(ecreds)

#1 Request acccess to data resource in Eratos
max_temp_data = eadapter.Resource(ern='ern:e-pn.io:resource:eratos.blocks.silo.maxtemperature')
min_temp_data = eadapter.Resource(ern='ern:e-pn.io:resource:eratos.blocks.silo.mintemperature')
rainfall_data = eadapter.Resource(ern='ern:e-pn.io:resource:eratos.blocks.silo.dailyrainfall')
#2 Convert resource object into gridded data object
gridded_max_temp_data = max_temp_data.data().gapi()
gridded_min_temp_data = min_temp_data.data().gapi()
gridded_rainfall_data = rainfall_data.data().gapi()

#3 Print variables so we know how to access the specfic variables
print(dict.keys(gridded_max_temp_data.variables()))
print(dict.keys(gridded_min_temp_data.variables()))
print(dict.keys(gridded_rainfall_data.variables()))

# 1
startDate = "2017-01-01"
endDate = "2021-12-31"
# 2
date_generated_list = pd.date_range(startDate, endDate, freq="Y")
date_range = date_generated_list.strftime("%Y").to_list()
print((date_range))


# Properties in Australia,  Mornington Pensiula, Lindsay Point and the Barossa Valley
point_names =['Mornington', 'Lindsay Point' ,'Barossa']
point_list = ['POINT(145.133716 -38.281493)','POINT(140.995874 -34.072670)','POINT(138.924527 -34.516368)']

#Query Dataset to Extract desired data
# max_temp, as found in the dataset variables
extracted_max_temp_data = gridded_max_temp_data.get_timeseries_at_points('max_temp', point_list, startDate, endDate)
# min_temp, as found in the dataset variables
extracted_min_temp_data = gridded_min_temp_data.get_timeseries_at_points('min_temp', point_list, startDate, endDate)
# daily_rain, as found in the dataset variables
extracted_rainfall_data = gridded_rainfall_data.get_timeseries_at_points('daily_rain', point_list, startDate, endDate)

# Set threshold values
max_temp_threshold = 36
min_temp_threshold = 2

# Create lists to store data for visuaisations
days_above_max_threshold = []
days_below_min_threshold = []
peak_temp_list = []
lowest_temp_list = []
max_rainfall_list = []
points_annual_rainfall_list = []

#days above threshold
# Iterate through all days collected and aggregate  to statistics interested in:
# Days above max_temp_threshold 
for i in range(extracted_max_temp_data.shape[0]):
    peak_temp_list.append(np.amax(extracted_max_temp_data[i]))
    arr = extracted_max_temp_data[i] >= max_temp_threshold
    annual_arr = np.split(arr[0:-1],len(date_range))
    above_temp_list = []
    for year in annual_arr:
        above_temp_list.append(year.sum())
    days_above_max_threshold.append(above_temp_list)

# Iterate through all days collected and aggregate to statistics interested in:
# Days below min_temp_threshold 
for i in range(extracted_min_temp_data.shape[0]):
    lowest_temp_list.append(np.amin(extracted_min_temp_data[i]))
    arr = extracted_min_temp_data[i] <= min_temp_threshold
    annual_arr = np.split(arr[0:-1],len(date_range))
    below_temp_list = []
    for year in annual_arr:
        below_temp_list.append(year.sum())
    days_below_min_threshold.append(below_temp_list)

# Iterate through all days collected and aggregate to statistics interested in:
# Annual rainfall:
for i in range(extracted_rainfall_data.shape[0]):
    print(i)
    max_rainfall_list.append(np.amax(extracted_rainfall_data[i]))
    arr = extracted_rainfall_data[i]
    annual_arr = np.split(arr[0:-1],len(date_range))
    mean_annual_rainfall_list = []
    for year in annual_arr:
        mean_annual_rainfall_list.append(year.sum())
    points_annual_rainfall_list.append(mean_annual_rainfall_list)


# Create dataframe 
data_dict = {"Farm":point_names,"Max_temp_all_years":peak_temp_list,"Min_temp_all_years":lowest_temp_list,"Max_Daily_Rainfall_all_years":max_rainfall_list}
data_frame = pd.DataFrame(data_dict)
print(tabulate(data_frame.head(), headers='keys', tablefmt='fancy_grid'))


#visualise mean annual rainfall

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
x = np.arange(len(date_range))  # the label locations
width = 0.25  # the width of the bars
#print(points_mean_annual_rainfall_list)
round_points_annual_rainfall_list_0 = [round(num, 2) for num in points_annual_rainfall_list[0]]
round_points_annual_rainfall_list_1 = [round(num, 2) for num in points_annual_rainfall_list[1]]
round_points_annual_rainfall_list_2 = [round(num, 2) for num in points_annual_rainfall_list[2]]

rects1 = ax.bar(x - width, round_points_annual_rainfall_list_0, width, label=point_names[0])
rects2 = ax.bar(x , round_points_annual_rainfall_list_1, width, label=point_names[1])
rects3 = ax.bar(x + width,round_points_annual_rainfall_list_2, width, label=point_names[2])

ax.set_ylabel(f'Annual Rainfall (MM)')
ax.set_title(f'Annual Rainfall (MM) across Farms')
ax.set_xticks(x, date_range)
ax.legend()
ax.bar_label(rects1, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects2, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects3, padding=3)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

#days above threshold Visulisation

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

rects1 = ax.bar(x - width, days_above_max_threshold[0], width, label=point_names[0])
rects2 = ax.bar(x , days_above_max_threshold[1], width, label=point_names[1])
rects3 = ax.bar(x + width, days_above_max_threshold[2], width, label=point_names[2])

ax.set_ylabel(f'Number of Days above {str(max_temp_threshold)} Degrees C')
ax.set_title(f'Days above {str(max_temp_threshold)} Degrees C across Farms')
ax.set_xticks(x, date_range)
ax.legend()
ax.bar_label(rects1, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects2, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects3, padding=3)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

#days below threshold visualisation
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

rects1 = ax.bar(x - width, days_below_min_threshold[0], width, label=point_names[0])
rects2 = ax.bar(x , days_below_min_threshold[1], width, label=point_names[1])
rects3 = ax.bar(x + width, days_below_min_threshold[2], width, label=point_names[2])

ax.set_ylabel(f'Number of Days below {str(min_temp_threshold)} Degrees C')
ax.set_title(f'Days below {str(min_temp_threshold)} Degrees C across Farms')
ax.set_xticks(x, date_range)
ax.legend()
ax.bar_label(rects1, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects2, padding=3)
ax.bar_label(rects3, padding=3)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Get rainfall data at a location for a specific time period

Source: https://docs.eratos.com/recipes/get-rainfall-data-at-a-location-for-a-specific-time-period.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.eratos.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Get rainfall data at a location for a specific time period

```python Python
import datetime
from datetime import timezone
import pandas as pd
from shapely import wkt, geometry
from eratos.creds import AccessTokenCreds
from eratos.adapter import Adapter
from eratos.resource import Resource
import time
from shapely import wkt, geometry
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
	
# Please input your credientials
ecreds = AccessTokenCreds(
  <key>,
  <secret>
)
eadapter = Adapter(ecreds)

#1 Request acccess to data resource in Eratos
rainfall_data = eadapter.Resource(ern='ern:e-pn.io:resource:YY36TGCQLUDLUZOYO6EOQ7MR')
#2 Convert resource object into gridded data object
gridded_rainfall_data = rainfall_data.data().gapi()
#3 Query the dataset to see whats inside
print(gridded_rainfall_data.variables())
#{'lat': {'dataType': 'f8', 'space': 'lat'}, 'lon': {'dataType': 'f8', 'space': 'lon'},
# 'time': {'dataType': 'f8', 'space': 'time'}, 'daily_rain': {'dataType': 'f4', 'space': 'daily_rain'}}


#1 YYYYMMDD
startDate = "2022-01-01"
endDate = "2022-05-01"
#Start & End date as a tuple
startEndDate = (startDate,endDate)

#2 Convert strings to datetime objects for pandas
start = datetime.datetime.strptime(startDate, "%Y-%m-%d")
end = datetime.datetime.strptime(endDate, "%Y-%m-%d")

#3 Generate calendar days between start and end
dates_generated = pd.date_range(start, end, freq='D')

#4 Take generated days and convert into list of YYYY-MM-DD Strings
date_range_list = dates_generated.strftime("%Y-%m-%d").tolist()

# key: Well Know Text format (WKT); Eratos standard
loc_dict = {'Sydney':'POINT(151.215012 -33.857697)','Melbourne':'POINT(144.968229 -37.817972)',
'Brisbane':'POINT(153.033500 -27.458882)','Adelaide':'POINT(138.599774 -34.926943)',
'Perth':'POINT(115.829267 -31.964286)','Canberra':'POINT(149.125937 -35.306481)',
'Darwin':'POINT(130.835612 -12.451164)'}

def rainfall_slice_extractor(gridded_rainfall_data, location, startEndDate):
    
    loc_shape = wkt.loads(location)
    if type(loc_shape) is not geometry.Point:
         raise ValueError('location should be a point')
    
    #2 date: Create a Unix timestamp in UTC timezone from the DD-MM-YYYY-MM formatted date string - e.g. "01-01-2022"
    unix_ts_utc_start = datetime.datetime.strptime(startEndDate[0], '%Y-%m-%d').replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp()
    unix_ts_utc_end = datetime.datetime.strptime(startEndDate[1], '%Y-%m-%d').replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp()
    
    #3
    times = gridded_rainfall_data.get_subset_as_array('time')
    start_idx = np.where(times == unix_ts_utc_start)[0][0]
    end_idx = (np.where(times == unix_ts_utc_end)[0][0])+1
    #4
    daily_rainfall_list = gridded_rainfall_data.get_point_slices('daily_rain', 'SPP', pts=[[loc_shape.y, loc_shape.x]], starts=[start_idx], ends=[end_idx])
    
    return daily_rainfall_list
  
# Plot Melbounre Daily data
clrs = ['b-', 'g-', 'r-', 'k-', 'm-', 'y-', 'c-']
point = loc_dict['Melbourne']
rainfall_list = rainfall_slice_extractor(gridded_rainfall_data, point, startEndDate)

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.plot(dates_generated,rainfall_list[0],clrs[0],label='Melbourne')
plt.ylabel("Rainfall")
plt.xlabel("Day")
plt.legend()
plt.xlim([dates_generated[0], dates_generated[-1]])

# Plot captial cities monthly data
plot_dict = {}
plot_dict['Date'] = dates_generated
for loc in loc_dict:

    point = loc_dict[loc]
    rainfall_list = rainfall_slice_extractor(gridded_rainfall_data, point, startEndDate)
    plot_dict[loc] = rainfall_list[0]


plot_df = pd.DataFrame(plot_dict,index=None)
plot_df.set_index('Date', inplace=True)
plot_df.index = pd.to_datetime(plot_df.index)
plot_df = plot_df.resample('1M').mean()

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
count = 0
print(plot_df)
for col in plot_df.columns:
    plt.plot(plot_df.index.values,plot_df[col].values,clrs[count],label=col)
    count+= 1

plt.ylabel("Mean Monthly Rainfall")
plt.xlabel("Month")
plt.legend()
plt.xlim([plot_df.index.values[0], plot_df.index.values[-1]])
plt.show()  
  
  

```

3. Access time dimension of dataset (UTC UNIX), at its intervals, index from the earliest time of the data [0] to the latest record [-1]
4. The API function get point slices does all the heavy lifting, and returns the slice of time we defined
